findings.problem: The rule that makes Hamming work (each check bit is chosen so its group holds an even number of 1s) is never stated while it happens. Each group gets about 1.6 s: rings, chips, a counter reading 'p4 even 2' / 'p2 odd 3', then the '?' becomes the bit. The counter label is cryptic (it does not say 2 and 3 are counts of 1s among the data bits; scene 3 called the same thing 'ones'), the captions only say what each check 'guards', and 'even count' first appears in the last caption (10.6). A first-time learner sees a bit appear and cannot tell how it was chosen; p2 going from 'odd 3' to 'even 4' by adding a 1 is the key step and is the quickest. The counter also sits about 200 px below its strip while only one group is on screen.
findings.fix: Reuse scene 3's wording: counter label 'ones' plus a small badge 'even: check bit 0' / 'odd: check bit 1'. Put the rule into caption 3 or 4, e.g. 'p4 guards 4-7; its bit makes the 1s even.' (8 words). Give each group about 2.3 s (tighten the legend slot 1.1-4.2 and the 2.6-3.5 binary fade, and use the 1.4 s end hold). Move the counter next to its strip.
findings.evidence: s8@5.5 and s8@5.9 (counter 'p4 even 2', '?' chip, caption names only the positions), s8@7.5 ('p2 odd 3' in orange), s8@9.5; captions at 4.9, 6.7, 8.8 never mention even/odd.

findings.problem: The headline says 'The receiver repeats the division' but nothing is divided on screen: a purple arrow labelled 'divide by 1101' and the remainder tiles just pop in as 000 / 111 / 110. The XOR rows were shown once, in scene 4, so a first-time learner cannot see why a clean frame leaves 000 or why a flip changes the answer; it looks like a lookup, not a calculation. (The reason 000 means clean is not on screen or in a caption either.)
findings.fix: Replay a compressed division for the clean frame at about 1.4-3.0 s: the two XOR rows of scene 4 (1011100 -> 0110100 -> 0000000), small, beside or under the frame, ending in the green 000. The two-flip and burst runs can stay as arrow plus result. If time is tight, change the badge text 'clean' to 'divides exactly' so the reason is on screen.
findings.evidence: s5@2.0 and s5@2.8 (arrow, 000, no rows), s5@3.6, s5@7.5; scene 4 rows at s4@7.4 for comparison.

findings.problem: While each new word is being checked the old verdict badge is kept at 35% opacity (PENDING, V.show(badgeBox, 1 - 0.65 * pend)). So for 1.5 s (3.0-4.5) and 1.7 s (6.0-7.7) a pale green 'clean' badge with a tick sits beside red flipped tiles, and at 7.5 beside a red 110 remainder while the caption already says 'A burst of three is caught too.' A first-time learner reads the ghost as a contradictory verdict, and it dims text to 0.35, far below the 0.8 house floor (whole-group fade, but the text still reads washed out).
findings.fix: Hide the badge while a word is pending (badge('none', 0) between the first flip and the verdict) or swap it for a neutral grey pill 'checking'. Keep every shown verdict at full opacity.
findings.evidence: s5@3.6 and s5@7.5 (pale 'clean' next to red tiles / red 110); opacity scan: 'clean' at 0.35 for 11 consecutive 0.25 s samples.

findings.problem: The payoff of the scene, that the same two flips that fooled parity in scene 3 are caught by the CRC, is on screen for about 1 s: remainder 111 appears at 3.8-4.4, 'error found' at 4.5-4.9, and the frame heals from 5.4. Nothing says these are the same flips (tiles 1 and 4), so 'Even two flips' leans on memory from 24 s earlier, and 'error found' is at full strength only about 0.5 s before the picture changes.
findings.fix: Hold the 111 / 'error found' state until about 6.2 (shift the heal, burst and rule tags by +0.8 s; the scene has a 1.4 s end hold) and add a small tag under the received row at about 3.3, e.g. 'the flips that fooled parity' (28 px, red outline), fading out with the heal.
findings.evidence: s5@4.6 and s5@4.8 (badge just arrived), s5@5.9 (heal under way); constants VERDICTS and STEPS in scene-05-check.js.

findings.problem: After step 2 the last row reads 0000 100: a 1 still sits in column 4 and the caption has just said 'Line the pattern up under the next 1', so a first-time learner expects a third step and cannot see why the division stops (fewer than four bits remain, so 1101 no longer fits). 'add 000' is likewise unexplained (one zero per check bit), so three check bits look arbitrary.
findings.fix: Caption 4 (8.0-9.7): 'Too short to divide again: that is the remainder.' (or 'Fewer than four bits left: remainder.'), and/or a grey tag 'too short for 1101' beside the remainder tag at about 7.9. Extend the tag to 'add 000: one per check bit' (there is room left of x 352).
findings.evidence: s4@7.4 (0000100 with the step-2 caption still on), s4@8.5; s4@4.0 ('add 000' tag only).

findings.problem: The headline 'One check bit catches one flip' and the last caption 'Two flips cancel out: missed.' teach 'one flip yes, two flips no'. The picture contradicts 'cancel out': both flips are 0 -> 1, the counter goes 4, 5, 6 and never returns to 4; only its evenness returns. A first-time learner will also infer that three flips slip through (the lesson: any odd number is caught, any even number missed).
findings.fix: Caption 5 (10.7-12.4): 'Two flips make it even again: missed.' or 'An even number of flips is missed.' Optionally retitle 'A parity bit catches odd flips'. Keep the picture.
findings.evidence: s3@4.5 (4), s3@6.8 (5, odd: alarm), s3@11.3 (6, green 'even: looks fine', 'missed').

findings.problem: Captions run ahead of their pictures. Caption 4 'Nearest valid word is 000: fixed.' opens at 9.2 but the repair is the token hopping back at about 9.65-10.2 (green ring 10.2-10.5): at 9.5 the token still sits above red 010. Caption 5 'Two flips lead to the wrong word.' opens at 11.8 but the wrong repair is the hop to 111 at about 12.05-12.55: at 11.9 the token is still on 011.
findings.fix: Caption 4 -> [9.6, 11.2]; caption 5 -> [12.1, 13.8]. The decoder tags stay on screen, so nothing is lost.
findings.evidence: s7@9.5 and s7@11.9 (caption on, token not yet moved); s7@10.4 and s7@12.4 (repair done).

findings.problem: Nothing bridges the cube to Hamming. Scene 7 ends on '3 apart fixes one flip' for the code 0 = 000, 1 = 111; scene 8 then opens with seven tiles and 'Check bits sit at positions 1, 2, 4.' The word 'Hamming' appears only in the 24 px kicker (and in scene 10's caption). A first-time learner asks 'why not just send everything three times?' and sees the cube idea dropped rather than continued; the lesson answers with the rate (1 useful bit in 3 against 4 in 7), and A6.RATE is computed and asserted in common.js but no scene uses it.
findings.fix: Open scene 8 with one grey tag over the tiles, e.g. 'Hamming code: 4 data bits + 3 check bits' (0.3-3.0 s), or make caption 1 'Hamming: 3 check bits guard 4 data bits.' In scene 7's end hold (13.0-14.0) add the grey tag '3 copies: 1 useful bit in 3' from A6.RATE.repeat, and in scene 8's hold a green tag '4 useful bits in 7' from A6.RATE.hamming.
findings.evidence: s7@13.4 (end state has no cost information), s8@0.3 and s8@1.5 (no mention of Hamming or of why 7 bits); grep RATE videos/a6/scene-*.js finds nothing.

findings.problem: Recap card 2 ('Far-apart valid words let us fix a flip') shows four dots, three purple arcs and a green tick floating above the second dot. Nothing shows a flip being repaired (no hop back to the green end), the three steps are unlabelled, and the tick reads as decoration. Cards 1 and 3 are self-explanatory pictures.
findings.fix: Draw the cube idea in miniature: after the arcs, a red dot on the second node with a short green curved arrow back to the first green node (the repair), and a '3 apart' label (28 px); hold the finished state as now. Keep the tick only on the repaired dot.
findings.evidence: s11@6.2 (tick drawing), s11@7.2 and s11@8.9 (final card 2).

findings.problem: The closing claim 'More check bits catch longer bursts' (9.0-10.8) is carried by two text pills, '3 check bits: every burst up to 3' and '16 check bits: every burst up to 16'. The 3 has a visual link (a 0.4 s pulse of the remainder tiles); the 16 has none, so the last 3 s are a bullet list over the burst picture.
findings.fix: Under the pills draw three orange tiles with a 3-long red bracket, then a long row of 16 small tiles (about 48 px, 6 px gap) with a 16-long bracket, so burst length against check bits is seen. Keep the pills as labels.

findings.problem: 'minutes away' is a loose tag at the top of the far-away panel (y about 636) while the long lane it describes is at y about 750, and the proof that waiting is too slow arrives late: caption 3 'A probe far away cannot wait.' opens at 6.4, but until the dotted return arrow and the 'too slow' tag at about 8.3-9.7 the only evidence is the dotted lane. 'too slow' is gone by 10.7, so the final frame does not say why the probe repairs itself.
findings.fix: Put 'minutes away' on the lane (a double-headed dimension line with the tag centred on it), start caption 3 at about 7.4 or bring the return arrow forward, and keep 'too slow' until the repair at about 10.4.
findings.evidence: s6@6.5 and s6@7.5 (loose tag, caption already on), s6@9.7 ('too slow'), s6@10.7 (gone).

findings.problem: The closing tags '1 flip: 112 of 112 fixed' and '2 flips: 0 of 336 fixed' are text only and unexplained (112 = 16 codewords x 7 positions, 336 = 16 x 21 pairs), so they read as arbitrary big numbers. Earlier the tag 'Position 7 was correct' (8.8) is green, the colour of good news, although it reports damage.
findings.fix: Label the counts, e.g. 'every word, every single flip: 112 of 112' and 'every word, every pair: 0 of 336' (they fit in 936 px at 28 px), or simplify to 'every single flip fixed' / 'no double flip fixed'. Make 'Position 7 was correct' grey or orange and keep green for 'fixed'.

findings.problem: The dashed orange slot at the end of the sent row pops at 0.8 s and sits empty and unexplained for about 8 s (it has no lane, while the seven message tiles do), then becomes 'check bit' at 8.7. A first-time learner is left wondering what the empty box is.
findings.fix: Bring the ghost slot in only when the sent row returns at about 8.0 (so it is explained within a second), or keep it but add a short dashed lane so it reads as 'room for one more bit'.
findings.evidence: s2@2.0 and s2@4.0 (empty dashed slot, no lane), s2@9.2 (becomes the check bit).

findings.problem: The same event has five names ('caught' and 'odd: alarm' in scene 3, 'error found' in scene 5, 'check fails' in scene 6, 'odd: failed' and 'failed checks' in scene 9). The words 'detection' and 'correction' from the title never label the two halves, and 'CRC' is named only by the 24 px kicker 'THE CRC' in scene 4 before the recap uses it as an item ('parity, CRC').
findings.fix: Use 'check fails' / 'fixed' consistently in the badges (s3 'odd: alarm' -> 'odd: check fails', s5 'error found' -> 'check fails'). Change the kickers to DETECTING (scenes 3-5) and CORRECTING (scenes 7-10) so the title's two words mean something. Add a solid orange 'CRC' tag beside the remainder in scene 4 or caption 1 'The CRC: a pattern both sides know.'
findings.evidence: kickers on s3..s10; badges at s3@6.8, s5@4.8, s6@3.5, s9@7.5; recap card 1 at s11@8.2.
